title: After eating, why should I go?
odia:
ଖାଇ ସାରିଲେ ଗାଈ କି ଯିବି
ଖାଇ ସାରିଲି କାହିଁକି ଯିବି?
literal_meaning: Once I have eaten, I will go to the cow. I have finished eating—why should I go?
meaning_odia: ଖାଇବା ପୂର୍ବରୁ ଗାଈ ପାଖକୁ ଯିବାର କଥା ଦେଉଛି; ଖାଇସାରିଲା ପରେ କାହିଁକି ଯିବି ବୋଲି ଓଲଟା ପଚାରୁଛି। ନିଜ ସ୍ୱାର୍ଥ ପୂରଣ ହୋଇଗଲେ ଆଗର ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତିରୁ ଓହରିଯିବାକୁ ଉତ୍ସର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଇଙ୍ଗିତ କରେ।
explanation: Before the meal, eating is presented as the condition for going. After the meal, the same speaker questions any need to go at all. The inspected source gloss reads this as withdrawing once one’s own purpose has been served. The small change from “once I have eaten” to “I have eaten” exposes the broken promise.
usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone promises to help carry supplies after receiving their meal. Once served, they refuse to help. A companion quotes the saying to recall the promise made before eating.
cultural_context: The cow gives the promise a concrete destination. Repeating eating and going in both lines makes the reversal sharp: the meal first delays the undertaking and then becomes the point after which it is abandoned.

witnesses.locator: Page13, two lines beginning ଖାଇ ସାରିଲେ.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026. Retains separated ଗାଈ କି and line breaks, without correction.
Matching wording with joined ଗାଈକି and ଖାଇସାରିଲି. Explicit gloss supports withdrawal after self-interest is satisfied; no specific cow-related task is named.

odia_summary: ନିଜ କାମ ସରିଗଲେ ଆଗର ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତିରୁ ଓହରିଯିବା।
english_summary: Withdrawing a promise once one’s own need has been met.
